headline: 3 detained as 13-year-old boy found dead near Comilla University
summary: The victim, Ishiat Shahriar Opratim, was the only son of a Comilla University professor. Police have recovered his mother's iPhone from a suspect's house.
details: 13-year-old Ishiat Shahriar Opratim, a Class VII student at Comilla Border Guard Public School, was found dead near Comilla University on Saturday afternoon.
Opratim had gone missing on Friday afternoon after telling his parents he was going out to take photographs with his mother's iPhone.

The victim's mother's iPhone, which Opratim was carrying, was recovered from the house of one of the suspects, Tuhin.

caption:
A 13-year-old boy went missing while taking photos; 24 hours later, his body was found.

13-year-old Ishiat Shahriar Opratim, a Class VII student at Comilla Border Guard Public School, was found dead near Comilla University on Saturday afternoon.

Opratim had gone missing on Friday afternoon after telling his parents he was going out to take photographs with his mother's iPhone.

His body was recovered from the Sananda hillocks on the outskirts of the city, nearly 24 hours after he disappearance.

Police have since detained three young men, identified as Tuhin, Anas, and Fahim, aged between 18 and 20, in connection with the alleged killing.

The victim's mother's iPhone, which Opratim was carrying, was recovered from the house of one of the suspects, Tuhin.

The victim was the only son of Nahida Begum, an associate professor of Bangla at Comilla University and businessman KM Firoz Shahriar.

Police are currently analyzing CCTV footage and questioning the suspects to determine the exact circumstances of the death.

Cumilla Superintendent of Police Anisuzzaman is expected to provide a further briefing on the investigation's progress.

Source: Prothom Alo, The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV

headline: Ctg: Police deny crude bomb blasts after explosion sounds heard
summary: Authorities in Chattogram city's Bakalia area report that reports of crude bomb detonations are merely rumours following sounds of explosions on Saturday night.
details: Sounds of explosions were heard on a road in Chattogram city’s Bakalia area on Saturday night, sparking concerns of crude bomb attacks.
A video purportedly showing crude bomb explosions surfaced on social media, showing the incident taking place around 11:00pm near Liza Community Club in the Kalamiya Bazar area.
However, the Chattogram Metropolitan Police (CMP) have officially denied that any crude bombs were detonated in the area.
Habibur Rahman Pramanik, deputy commissioner (South) of the CMP, stated that the reports are rumours and no such explosions took place.
Police teams from various stations are currently deployed in the field to prevent sabotage and ensure public safety.
caption:
Explosion sounds in Chattogram? Police say it's just a rumour.

Sounds of explosions were heard on a road in Chattogram city’s Bakalia area on Saturday night, sparking concerns of crude bomb attacks.

A video purportedly showing crude bomb explosions surfaced on social media, showing the incident taking place around 11:00pm near Liza Community Club in the Kalamiya Bazar area.

However, the Chattogram Metropolitan Police (CMP) have officially denied that any crude bombs were detonated in the area.

Habibur Rahman Pramanik, deputy commissioner (South) of the CMP, stated that the reports are rumours and no such explosions took place.

Police teams from various stations are currently deployed in the field to prevent sabotage and ensure public safety.

#Chattogram #Bangladesh #News #CMP #PublicSafety

Source: The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune
